description:
Integrity Martial Arts runs children's classes from its base in Dungarvan Shopping Centre, Co. Waterford, with training built around clear belt progression so kids can see their own improvement over time.

Alongside the physical side — coordination, discipline and fitness — sessions place equal weight on mindfulness and self-control, values that carry over well beyond the training floor.

The club emphasises community as much as technique, with children training alongside peers in a supportive, encouraging setting.

Tramore Pottery offers two hand-building pottery programmes for children at Riverstown Community Centre in Tramore, Co. Waterford, both running on Tuesdays.

Kids Pottery Classes are aimed at ages 6-11, introducing basic clay techniques like pinch pots, coiling and slab work in a relaxed, sensory-rich setting. Clay Club, for the 10-14 age group, builds on those foundations with more independent, detailed projects.

Working with clay gives children a tactile break from screens while developing patience, fine motor control and a real sense of achievement in finishing a piece.

Primal Fitness in Drogheda's Greenhills Industrial Village runs a Junior Brazilian Jiu Jitsu programme for children aged 5 to 9, with classes held three times a week on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 4:30pm.

Each 45-minute session works on the grappling fundamentals of BJJ — balance, positional awareness and problem-solving on the mat — while building fitness and focus appropriate to younger children.

A free trial class is available before committing, with ongoing membership priced at €65 per month.

Black Belt Ireland runs its Kids Karate classes at Holy Family Community Centre in Drogheda every Sunday at 1:30pm.

Instruction is led by Peter Sheeran, a 2nd Dan black belt with the World Karate Confederation, giving children a structured introduction to karate technique, discipline and respect within a traditional club setting.

Weekly sessions offer a steady, low-pressure way for kids to build fitness, focus and confidence over time.

Creative Circle has been running art-based programmes for children in the Boyne Room at Millmount, Drogheda since 2018, offering both school-holiday camps and regular Saturday drop-in classes.

Groups are organised by age — 5 to 8, 8 to 11 and 11 to 15 — so activities and techniques are pitched appropriately as children's fine motor skills and creative interests develop.

The drop-in format at Millmount suits families looking for flexible, no-long-term-commitment art sessions alongside camp options during school breaks.

Fun with French brings French language classes to children aged 2 to 13 in Drogheda and the surrounding area, using the La Jolie Ronde method — a programme built around songs, games and repetition suited to young learners.

Classes are kept in small groups, which helps keep sessions interactive and gives each child more chances to speak and be heard.

Starting a second language early is widely recognised for building listening skills and cognitive flexibility, and the playful, low-pressure format here is designed to keep children engaged rather than drilled.

Kidkast Performing Arts School has been family-run since 1998, teaching Ballet, Modern, Drama, Musical Theatre and Acrobatic Arts to children from its base at Old Abbey Dance Studios on Old Abbey Lane, Drogheda, as well as satellite locations in Collon and Garristown.

The broad curriculum lets children try several performing arts disciplines rather than committing to just one, building coordination, musicality and stage confidence along the way.

With over two decades of continuous teaching in the area, the school has an established structure for progressing students from beginner classes through to more advanced performance work.

The Red Dragon Martial Arts Club teaches children's karate at Holy Family Community Centre in Ballsgrove, Drogheda, with weekly Sunday classes running from 1:30 to 2:30pm for ages 7 to 17.

Karate training at this stage focuses on developing coordination, self-discipline and respect for others, alongside practical self-defence skills built up gradually through structured technique work.

New members can try their first class for free, with ongoing sessions priced at €7 per class — a low-commitment way to see if the club is the right fit.

Dundalk School of Music runs a Pre-instrumental course for children aged 4 to 6 at its Blackthorn Business Park premises on Coe's Road, Dundalk, designed as a gentle first step before picking up an actual instrument.

The 9-week programme uses group activities, movement and rhythm work to build the listening skills, pulse and coordination that later instrumental lessons rely on.

It's a natural starting point for young children showing an interest in music, giving them a taste of group learning before moving on to individual tuition.

Dundalk Yoga Collective offers children's yoga in two formats: weekly term-time classes for ages 6 and up, held Mondays from 4:20 to 5pm, and five-day Holiday Kids Yoga Camps during school breaks, priced at €100.

Kids' yoga sessions combine playful movement with breathing and relaxation exercises, helping children build body awareness, focus and a healthy outlet for excess energy.

The camp format gives children a more immersive week-long introduction, while the term-time class suits those wanting a regular, low-key weekly practice.

Elevate Dundalk runs Antigravity Yoga classes for children, using a soft aerial hammock to support poses and movements that would be difficult on the ground alone.

Multiple sessions run each week, giving children a fun, slightly unconventional alternative to mat-based yoga while still building core strength, flexibility and balance.

The suspended format tends to appeal particularly to kids who enjoy a physical challenge, turning core yoga principles into something closer to play.

Fun Gymnastics operates from Unit 3A at Northlink Retail Park in Dundalk, running both recreational and more advanced gymnastics classes for children aged 2 to 12 and up.

With classes scheduled six days a week, families have plenty of flexibility to find a slot that fits, whether a child is just starting out with basic tumbling and balance work or progressing into more advanced skills.

Gymnastics at this age builds strength, flexibility and body control that carries over into most other sports.

Navan School of Ballet teaches classical ballet and jazz to students of all ages, including children, from its studio at Unit 6 Beechmount, Homepark, Navan.

Students who want to work towards formal qualifications can enter ISTD or Irish Board of Dance exams, giving a structured progression path alongside the regular class syllabus.

Ballet in particular develops posture, discipline and musicality, while the jazz classes offer a more upbeat, energetic counterpart for children who enjoy a faster pace.

Meath Martial Arts runs a Kids Karate Club in Navan for children aged 3 to 10, split into two age bands: a shorter 45-minute class for 3 and 4 year olds, and a 55-minute session for children aged 5 to 10.

Splitting classes this way lets younger children work at a pace and attention span suited to their age, while older kids get a longer, more technique-focused session.

A free trial class is available, with ongoing membership starting from €50 per month.

Play & Music Meath runs parent-and-child music and sensory classes for babies and toddlers across Meath, including Navan, with three programmes to choose from: Baby Sensory Play, Baby Play & Music and Mixed Age Play & Music.

Each format blends songs, instruments and sensory exploration, giving very young children stimulating, age-appropriate input while also creating a regular social outing for parents and carers.

The Mixed Age option is useful for families with children of different ages who want to attend together rather than juggling separate class times.

Studio X in Bray runs weekly hip hop classes for children split into three age groups — 4 to 7, 8 to 12 and 12 and up — so choreography and pace can be matched to each stage of development.

During school holidays, the studio also runs summer camps for two further bands, 5 to 8 and 9 and up, giving kids a more intensive dance experience over the break.

Hip hop classes are a good fit for children who want a high-energy, music-driven style of dance rather than a more formal or classical approach.

The Dance Academy in Bray teaches ongoing ballet and jazz classes for children from tots through to teens at The Epworth Hall, with terms running for 10 weeks at a time.

Classes follow the RAD and ISTD syllabuses, giving students the option to work towards recognised dance exams as they progress through the school.

Term fees run from €90 to €120, covering a full ten weeks of weekly classes for whichever age group and style a child joins.

Active Ennis runs intensive summer swim lessons for children aged 4 and up, held on weekday mornings and priced at €50 per child per week.

The intensive format — daily lessons over a concentrated block rather than one class a week — suits children learning a new skill quickly, whether that's getting comfortable in water for the first time or moving up through the Beginners to Improver 2 levels.

It's a popular option for families looking to make real swimming progress over the summer break rather than a single weekly top-up.

Ennis Art School runs art classes for children and teens aged 5 to 18, split into three age bands (5-10, 10-14 and 14-18), based at St Flannan's College with an online option also available.

The curriculum covers drawing, painting, craft and animation, giving students a broad grounding across different media rather than specialising in just one from the start.

Having both in-person and online formats gives families flexibility, particularly useful for older students balancing art classes with other school and extracurricular commitments.

Ennis Gymnastics Club's Under 6s Programme offers drop-and-go gymnastics classes for the youngest members, split into Preschool (ages 3-4) and Mini Juniors (ages 5-6).

At this age, gymnastics focuses on fundamental movement skills — balance, coordination, spatial awareness — delivered through games and simple apparatus work rather than formal routines.

The drop-and-go format means parents don't need to stay for the class, making it a straightforward addition to a young child's weekly routine.

Ennis Hockey Club welcomes both boys and girls from age 5 into its junior hockey sessions, with trial sticks provided so complete beginners can try the sport before investing in their own equipment.

The club describes its junior set-up as friendly and inclusive, aiming to introduce children to hockey's stick skills, teamwork and match play in a relaxed environment rather than a heavily competitive one.

It's a good entry point for children who haven't played hockey before, with equipment support removing one of the usual barriers to giving a new sport a try.

Kells Tennis Club in Co. Meath runs junior tennis camps during school holidays, with sessions timed around Halloween, Easter and summer breaks.

Camps run with daily instruction across the week, giving children a concentrated block of coaching to build stroke technique, footwork and match awareness rather than a single weekly lesson.

Prices range from €50 to €65 depending on the camp, making it an accessible way for kids in Kells to try tennis or build on existing skills during time off school.

Tribe Art Studio, based at Unit 4 Kennedy Street in Carlow, runs children's art and pottery classes throughout the year alongside seasonal camps during school holidays.

Classes are open to all ages and abilities, so both children with no previous experience and those wanting to develop existing skills can take part.

Combining two-dimensional art with hands-on pottery gives children a mix of drawing and painting work alongside more tactile, three-dimensional making within the same studio.

Little VISUAL is an early-years music workshop for toddlers aged 18 months to 3 years, run at VISUAL Carlow on the Old Dublin Road every Tuesday from 10 to 11am, with an accompanying adult required.

Sessions use music and movement to engage very young children's developing senses, while also giving parents and carers a shared, sociable activity to attend together.

At €5 per adult-and-child pair, it's a low-cost, drop-in-friendly way to introduce toddlers to rhythm and sound in an arts-centre setting.

Sunshine Pottery runs a 4-week hand-building pottery course for children aged 6 and up at its Castle Gate premises in Carlow, taught by Jayne.

Over the four weeks, children work through hand-building techniques such as pinching, coiling and slab construction, giving them a complete arc from raw clay to a finished piece.

The short course format makes it a manageable commitment for families wanting to try pottery without signing up for a full term.

Kilkenny Gymnastics Academy offers a broad range of gymnastics programmes, starting with Mini Gym for children aged 3.5 to 5 and progressing through recreational and competitive streams as children get older.

Beyond core gymnastics, the academy also runs trampolining classes and GymABLE, a disability-inclusive programme designed to make gymnastics accessible to a wider range of children.

Having this range under one roof means children can move between streams — recreational, competitive, trampolining or GymABLE — as their interests and abilities develop, without having to change club.

Kilkenny Juvenile Fight Club runs Saturday kickboxing sessions for children and teens aged 6 to 16 at Kilkenny Combat Academy in the Hebron Industrial Estate, from 11am to 12:30pm.

The single weekly slot works well for families looking for a structured but not overly time-intensive martial arts commitment, covering kickboxing technique, fitness and discipline in one longer session.

New members can try their first class for free, with ongoing membership priced at €20 per month.

Art It Kilkenny runs term-based studio art classes covering a wide age range, from 4 up to 18, split across three distinct classes through the week.

Saturday Fun Art is aimed at ages 6-12, Thursday Fun Drawing at 8-13, and Friday Painting & Perspective is pitched at older students aged 9-18 wanting more technical, perspective-focused work.

Having classes spread across different days and skill levels means children can find a slot and style — playful drawing, structured art, or a more advanced painting focus — that suits where they're at.

Kilkenny Academy of Dance, based at the Smithlands Centre on Bohernatounish Road in Kilkenny Town, teaches ISTD ballet, contemporary/modern and jazz to children from age 3 upward.

The academy also runs a dedicated boys' hip hop class, offering an alternative style and a same-gender group setting for boys who might be less drawn to the traditional dance styles.

Summer camps run during school holidays, giving children an intensive dance-focused week outside the regular term-time schedule.

Dancewise Academy teaches dance and drama to children aged 4 and up across two venues: Dancewise Studios in Kilkenny on Tuesdays, and Castlecomer Community Hall on Wednesdays.

Combining dance and drama in the same programme gives children exposure to both movement-based and performance skills, useful preparation for anyone interested in musical theatre down the line.

Running classes in both Kilkenny and Castlecomer means families across a wider catchment area have a local session to choose from.

Krav Maga Kilkenny runs a kids' class for ages 6 to 11 focused on confidence, discipline and practical anti-bullying skills, with sessions available in Kilkenny on Mondays and Wednesdays, or in Clonmel on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

Krav Maga's practical, no-nonsense approach to self-defence is adapted here for a younger audience, prioritising awareness and confidence-building alongside physical technique.

Monthly membership runs from €30 to €50, with the choice of two locations giving families in either town a convenient class night.

SBG Naas offers children's Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in Co. Kildare, split into two age groups — 7 to 9 and 10 to 12 — so technique and intensity can be matched to each stage.

Alongside the BJJ classes, the gym also runs Growing Gorillas, a personal development programme that uses martial arts as a vehicle for building confidence, focus and resilience rather than purely competitive skill.

Together, the two programmes give parents a choice between a more traditional grappling-focused class and one with an explicit personal-development angle.

Naas Kickboxing and Fitness runs children's kickboxing classes in Naas, Co. Kildare, split by age: a Thursday class for 5 to 9 year olds, and more frequent sessions on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday for 10 to 16 year olds.

The extra weekly sessions available to the older group suit children wanting to train more regularly and progress technique faster, while the single weekly class for younger kids keeps things manageable for beginners.

Kickboxing builds cardiovascular fitness, coordination and discipline alongside striking technique, appealing to kids who want a more dynamic alternative to traditional martial arts.

Theatrics Naas runs drama and musical theatre classes for children and teens aged 5 to 17 at The Moat Theatre in Naas.

Working in an actual theatre venue gives students a genuine stage environment to build confidence in, whether they're working on acting technique, singing or the combined performing skills of musical theatre.

The wide age range, from young children through to older teens, allows students to progress through the programme over several years as their performance skills develop.

Bryan Carr School of Performing Arts runs a Saturday stage school for children aged 5 and up at Collis Sandes House in Oakpark, Tralee, covering singing, dance and acting in one combined programme.

Students get the chance to put those skills into practice in two annual musical productions staged at Siamsa Tíre, Tralee's national folk theatre — a notable performance outlet for a weekly stage school.

At around €6 an hour, the class offers a broad performing-arts grounding with a genuine public performance goal built into the year.

Tralee Sports Complex runs Pre-School and Parents & Tots swimming classes for children aged 3.5 to 5, giving very young swimmers a structured, age-appropriate introduction to the pool.

At this age, classes typically focus on water confidence, basic safety and simple skills like floating and blowing bubbles rather than formal stroke work, laying the groundwork for more structured lessons later.

Being based at a dedicated sports complex means access to proper pool facilities geared toward group children's lessons.

ARTlab Tralee runs art, craft and design classes for older children and teens aged 9 to 17, based near the Dingle road in Tralee.

Classes are organised into seven-week summer terms, with sessions held on Fridays and Saturdays, giving a concentrated run of classes over the school break rather than a year-round commitment.

Covering craft and design alongside traditional art gives slightly older students room to explore more varied, project-based creative work than a typical drawing-and-painting class.

Evolution Gym Tralee runs youth fitness classes for children and teens aged 7 to 18, split into two main tracks: one for ages 7-11, and another for 12-18.

Older teens have the additional option of a Sport Performance track, geared toward athletes wanting more targeted strength and conditioning work alongside general fitness.

A free trial class lets new members try the gym's youth programme before committing to ongoing membership.

Reel Beginnings, run by the Kingdom Academy of Irish Dance, introduces children aged 4 and up to Irish dance at two Tralee venues: St Johns Parish Centre and the Comhaltas Centre.

The beginner-focused class uses games to teach the basics, keeping young children engaged while building the fitness, rhythm and coordination that Irish dance relies on.

It's a gentle, low-pressure entry point for kids new to Irish dance, before they'd move on to more formal or competitive class structures.

Ready Set Achieve runs an 8-week preschool swim programme at Tralee Sports Complex, with hands-on instruction supporting young children through each stage of learning to swim.

The structured 8-week block gives a clear start and end point for progress, useful for parents wanting to track how their child is coming along.

Demand for places is currently high enough that the programme is waitlist-only, so interested families should register ahead of when they hope to start.

Super Stars Yoga runs children's yoga classes for ages 3 to 13 across several Tralee venues, including Banna Beach Leisure Centre and Collis Sandes House.

Running across multiple locations gives families more choice of a convenient class, and the wide age range means the same provider can be a fit for a child from preschool right through to early teens.

Beyond regular classes, Super Stars Yoga also delivers yoga workshops directly in schools, bringing mindfulness and movement into the classroom setting.

Tralee Gymnastics Club, based in Clahane, Ballyard, runs a full range of gymnastics classes from toddlers right through to advanced level.

Toddler classes for ages 2-4 involve a participating parent, easing children into the gym environment together, while Recreational classes from age 5 and an Advanced stream cater to children as their skills and confidence grow.

The club currently has a long waitlist, so families interested in joining should contact them directly to check on availability.

Tricia O'Connor runs afterschool classes in Tralee for children aged 4 to 11, blending art, nature and mindfulness into each session rather than treating them as separate activities.

Seasonal camps extend the same approach into school holiday periods, and for children who'd benefit from more individual attention, a 1:1 Art & Meditation option is also available.

Combining creative and calming activities in one class suits children who respond well to a slower-paced, reflective style of afterschool care alongside hands-on making.

Anne Maher School of Ballet runs weekly ballet classes across three towns — Naas, Newbridge and Trim — starting with Twinkle Toes for children from age 3.5.

From that starting class, students can progress through the school's structure as they get older, giving a long-term pathway rather than a single standalone class.

Having classes in three separate towns means families across a wider stretch of Kildare and Meath have a local option to choose from.

Fit Kids/Fit Teens runs Hip Hop classes for a broad age range, 3 to 16, on Tuesdays at Flemington Community Centre in Balbriggan.

The wide span means the class can work for a whole family with children of different ages, an aspect reinforced by the family discounts on offer alongside the standard €10-per-class rate.

Hip hop's upbeat, music-led style tends to appeal to kids looking for a more energetic, less formal alternative to classical dance training.

Flemington Community Centre in Balbriggan hosts a range of children's programmes under one roof, spanning dance schools, martial arts, Foroige youth groups, ballet and Mandarin classes.

Rather than a single class, the centre functions as a hub for several different providers, so families can find multiple activities for children of different interests and ages in the one venue.

Contacting the centre directly is the best way to check current schedules and availability for each individual programme.

JR Piano Lessons offers one-to-one piano tuition for children from age five through to teenagers, based at Hamptons Garden Avenue in Balbriggan, with the option of either in-studio or at-home lessons.

Individual lessons let the pace and material be tailored closely to each student, which can suit both complete beginners and those who've already started learning elsewhere.

The choice between studio and home lessons gives families flexibility around what fits best with their schedule and their child's comfort learning in a familiar setting.

WSKF SEDAI runs an after-school kids' karate club in Skerries, Co. Dublin, meeting Mondays and Wednesdays at 6:20pm, with additional sessions available in nearby Lusk and Balbriggan.

Having classes across three towns gives families flexibility to attend whichever location and evening suits best, while still training under the same club structure.

As an after-school activity, the timing works well for children going straight from school into a structured, active class rather than heading home first.

Balbriggan & District AC runs kids' athletics training on Monday evenings at Balbriggan Sports Centre, covering both a Little Athletes group for younger children and a Juveniles group for older kids.

Children who go on to compete have the option of an additional Wednesday session, giving more dedicated training time for those pursuing athletics more seriously.

Athletics at club level builds a broad base of running, jumping and throwing skills, useful groundwork whether or not a child goes on to specialise in a particular event.

Elite Taekwon-Do trains children and teens at Castleland Community Centre in Balbriggan, with classes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 6 to 6:45pm.

The programme is split into Young Warriors for ages 7-11 and Teen Warriors for 12 and up, keeping training partners and pacing appropriate to each group.

Taekwon-Do's emphasis on kicking technique, patterns and sparring gives children a structured, belt-graded path to work through as they build fitness and self-discipline.

Beyond Jiujitsu Academy in Balbriggan has run a dedicated kids' Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu programme since 2018, led by coaches focused specifically on youth training rather than adapting adult classes for children.

BJJ's grappling-based approach teaches children how to use leverage and technique rather than strength alone, building both physical skill and problem-solving under pressure.

Having youth-focused coaching in place from the start means classes are built around how children learn and engage, not just a scaled-down adult curriculum.

Castleland Community Centre in Balbriggan hosts a wide spread of children's activities under one roof, including Polish Folk Dance, art classes, GAA, volleyball, soccer, taekwondo and a theatre school.

With this many different programmes running from the same venue, it's a useful first stop for families in Balbriggan looking to find an activity without knowing exactly what they want to try yet.

Since providers and schedules vary, it's worth contacting the centre directly to confirm current class times for whichever activity interests your child.

Skerries Art School runs children's art classes at Skerries Mills, drawing families from across Skerries, Rush, Lusk, Balbriggan and Malahide.

Alongside the core children's classes, the school also offers exam support and portfolio preparation, making it a useful option for older students working toward formal art assessments as well as younger children just starting out creatively.

Covering both ends of that spectrum — playful early classes and serious exam prep — means students can stay with the same school as their art education becomes more advanced.

Club Vitae runs kids' group swim lessons from age 4, structured in 8-week blocks with classes on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays running from September through June, plus additional summer sessions.

The 8-week block structure gives clear check-in points to track a child's progress through swim levels, rather than an open-ended ongoing class.

With sessions available three days a week across most of the year, families have a good amount of flexibility in choosing a slot that fits their schedule.

Caroline Keane runs Junior Art Club (ages 7+) and Senior Art Club (ages 8+) in Portlaoise, with 7-week terms held between September and June at Dunamaise Arts Centre and Treo Nua.

Splitting into junior and senior clubs by roughly a year's difference in starting age lets projects and techniques be pitched a little differently for each group as children's skills develop.

Term fees are €80, with all materials included, so there's nothing extra for parents to source before a child starts.

Krav Maga Portlaoise & Midlands runs a kids' Krav Maga programme built around self-defence, discipline, confidence and general fitness, and has been growing steadily since 2018.

Krav Maga's practical, situation-based approach to self-defence is adapted for younger students, with an emphasis on awareness and confidence as much as physical technique.

The programme's growth since it started points to steady demand across the Portlaoise and Midlands area for this style of martial arts training for children.

Portlaoise Kenkyo Dojo teaches Irish Karate Kyokushinkai to children from age 4, split into a 4-6 group and a 7+ group, with classes on Wednesdays and Fridays at Portlaoise Parish Centre and Gaelscoil Phortlaoise.

Kyokushinkai is a full-contact style of karate, and splitting classes by age this way lets the intensity and contact level be adjusted appropriately for younger versus older children.

Running across two venues in Portlaoise gives some flexibility around which class night and location suits a family best.

Ninja Tots, held at Portlaoise Parish Centre on Stradbally Road, offers martial-arts-inspired play for children aged 2 to 7, led by coach Shane Culleton.

Rather than formal martial arts instruction, the class channels similar movement patterns — balance, coordination, controlled energy — into a playful format better suited to very young children.

It works well as an early stepping stone for kids who might move on to a more structured martial art once they're a bit older, while still being a complete, standalone activity in its own right.

Portlaoise Gymnastics Club's Gym Start class is aimed at children aged 5 and up, though 4-year-olds already in school can also join.

Classes are capped at a 1:8 coach-to-child ratio, keeping group sizes manageable, and children are introduced to the full range of gymnastics apparatus as part of the weekly class rather than working on just one piece at a time.

It's designed as a solid entry point into club gymnastics, giving young beginners a broad first exposure to the sport.

Speak Out Drama is an award-winning drama school in Portlaoise offering acting, singing and dance classes, with summer camps running during school holidays.

Students get the chance to perform at Dunamaise Arts Centre, giving the weekly classes a real performance outcome to work toward rather than just skills practice in the studio.

Combining all three performing arts disciplines — acting, singing and dance — in one school suits children interested in musical theatre or general stage confidence rather than a single specialism.

Aikyam.Yoga runs kids' yoga for ages 4 to 10 out of Garden Vale, Athlone, with a regular Saturday class at 10:15am in St Mary's Hall, plus Monday evening drop-in sessions during July and August.

The summer drop-in format gives families a flexible, no-commitment option to try a session or two over the holidays, at €5 per class, alongside the more structured Saturday class during the rest of the year.

Kids' yoga at this age blends playful movement with simple breathing exercises, giving children tools to self-regulate as well as basic flexibility and body awareness.

Athlone Gymnastics Club offers recreational gymnastics for beginners aged 6 and up, run on a drop-in basis rather than requiring a fixed weekly commitment.

Easter and summer camps run during school holidays and are open to both existing members and non-members, giving new families a chance to try the club without first signing up for term-time classes.

The drop-in structure suits children and parents who want flexibility around attendance rather than a rigid weekly schedule.

Athlone Taekwondo I.T.F.U. runs taekwondo and fitness classes for kids and youth across multiple locations, starting with Little Ninjas for ages 4 to 6.

Older children can progress into more competitive kickboxing training or focus on self-defence skills, giving a choice of direction as kids get older and their interests become clearer.

Running across several venues means the club can offer more class times and locations than a single-site school, useful for families across the wider Athlone area.

Athlone Regional Sports Centre's Swim For Life Child programme takes children aged 4 to 17 through a structured 10-level curriculum, giving a clear long-term progression from complete beginner up through more advanced stages.

A SwimFit option is also available for children who've completed the core levels and want to keep building fitness and stamina in the water.

Courses run for 12 weeks at a time, priced between €96 and €120 depending on the level and course chosen.

Kinder Stage School at Mullingar Arts Centre on Lower Mount Street introduces drama, dance and music to children aged 3 to 6, with sessions running on Mondays and Thursdays.

Combining all three disciplines in one early-years class gives very young children a varied, multi-sensory introduction to the performing arts rather than committing to a single discipline this early.

Being based at an established arts centre gives the class access to a proper performance-oriented space from the start.

Elevate Academy of Dance, now in its 19th year, teaches ballet, contemporary, jazz, acro-dance and musical theatre to children from age 4 across two studios in Mullingar.

Students who want to work toward formal qualifications can follow the ISTD exam pathway alongside their regular classes, giving a structured route through the various styles on offer.

Covering five distinct disciplines under one academy gives children room to specialise in whichever style suits them best, without needing to switch schools.

Lakeland Jiu Jitsu's Mullingar Youth Programme splits kids' Jiu Jitsu into two groups, ages 4-7 and 8-12, with classes running Monday, Wednesday and Saturday under black belt instructors.

Three sessions a week gives children more regular mat time than a typical once-weekly class, useful for building technique and confidence faster.

A free trial class is available, and the club also runs a summer camp during school holidays for a more intensive week of training.

An Grianán Youth Theatre runs Junior (ages 7-12) and Senior (ages 13-18) drama groups at An Grianán Theatre on Port Road, Letterkenny, across the September-to-June school year.

Being based in a working theatre gives members a genuine stage and production environment, rather than a classroom standing in for one.

The split between junior and senior groups allows young people to stay involved with the same theatre from childhood through to their late teens, moving up as they get older.

Citadel Gymnastics runs both recreational and competitive gymnastics from a purpose-built facility in Letterkenny, with a second base in Gweedore, catering to all ages and abilities.

The club uses adaptive equipment, making its classes accessible to children with a wider range of physical abilities than a standard gymnastics setup might accommodate.

Having a dedicated, purpose-built space is a notable feature for a gymnastics club, giving proper apparatus and training conditions rather than a shared multi-use hall.

Letterkenny Community Centre hosts a range of children's classes across the week, including junior soccer, gymnastics, martial arts (jiu jitsu and karate) and RINKA fitness.

With several different activities running from the one venue, it's a convenient option for families wanting to try different sports and classes without travelling between multiple locations.

Since each activity runs on its own weekly slot, it's worth checking with the centre for current timetables before choosing which class to join.

Mini Maestros is a 6-week early music class for children aged 4 to 6, held Tuesdays at 3:45pm at the Regional Cultural Centre on Cove Hill, Port Road, Letterkenny.

The class is run by the Donegal Music Education Partnership, giving it a grounding in established music education practice rather than a one-off activity class.

At €50 for the full 6-week block, it offers a short, structured first taste of group music-making for young children before they might move on to individual instrument lessons.

Pinehill Studios in Letterkenny runs a wide spread of after-school classes for children under one roof, including Hip Hop, Piano, Arts & Crafts, Irish Dancing, Ballet and Drama.

Having this many different activities in one venue means children — and their families — can try several interests without needing to travel between different providers across town.

Multi-activity camps run during school holidays, extending the same variety into a more intensive holiday format.

David Lewis Golf runs an after-school golf programme at Greystones Golf Course for ages 7 and up, running from September through May, along with Easter and summer camps during school holidays.

The programme attracts more than 140 juniors on a weekly basis, indicating a well-established junior golf community rather than a small standalone class.

Golf offers children a different pace and skill set to most team sports — patience, precision and etiquette alongside physical technique — and the after-school timing makes regular attendance straightforward during the school year.

Greystones Lawn Tennis Club on Mill Road runs its Junior Play N Stay sessions on Thursday afternoons, catering to various age groups within the one programme.

Non-members can try a free trial session before committing, with ongoing 12-week blocks priced between €24 and €48 depending on age group and membership status.

Play N Stay style coaching typically uses modified courts, balls and scoring to help younger or newer players rally and play points sooner than they could on a full-sized court.

Greystones Gymnastics Academy runs year-round girls' artistic gymnastics for ages 6-12, with both recreational and advanced streams available depending on a child's experience and goals.

For those aiming higher, a TEAM programme covers a wider age range, 7 to 17, giving a longer-term competitive pathway under coach Marcel.

The mix of recreational and TEAM options means the academy can support gymnasts who just want a fun weekly class as well as those pursuing more serious competitive training.

Greystones Languages for Children runs term-based Spanish and French classes for ages 5 to 13, held across several school venues in the Greystones area.

Offering both languages gives families a choice depending on a child's school curriculum or personal interest, and having classes at multiple local schools makes attendance straightforward without extra travel.

Term fees are €120, with each full term giving a sustained run of weekly lessons rather than a short taster course.

Greystones Taekwon-Do runs structured classes for children and teens aged 4 to 16, starting with a Kids Development Programme for the youngest members and progressing through to teen classes.

Sessions run on Wednesdays and Saturdays, giving a twice-weekly rhythm for regular skill-building without an overly heavy time commitment.

The programme's age-graded structure means children can stay with the same club as they grow, moving from early development work into more advanced Taekwon-Do training.

Kraftworx runs after-school crafting and sewing classes for children aged 6 and up, with a semester-based structure that lets skills build progressively rather than starting fresh each class.

The classes have a distinct upcycling focus, teaching children to turn materials into new, useful or decorative items — a slightly different angle to standard arts-and-crafts classes.

Greystones sessions run at around €100 per semester, covering a full run of weekly classes.

Yoga with Michelle runs Kids Yoga at St Patrick's Church on Church Road, Greystones, every Friday from 2:15 to 3:15pm.

Classes combine playful movement, simple breathwork and mindfulness exercises, giving children tools for both physical activity and self-regulation within the same hour.

The class runs in 4-week blocks priced at €50, a manageable commitment for families wanting to try kids' yoga without a long-term sign-up.

Bar Monkey Calisthenics, based at Ballyloughan Business Park on the Arklow Road in Gorey, runs age-graded calisthenics programmes spanning from 4-6 year olds right through to 14-16 year olds.

Alongside the standard age-group classes, dedicated statics and strength courses are available for children wanting to focus more specifically on bodyweight strength skills.

Calisthenics builds functional strength and body control using just bodyweight movement, an approach that scales naturally across this wide age range as children get stronger and more coordinated.

Innovations Theatre School teaches performing arts to children and teens aged 5 to 18, covering drama, dance and singing across three 10-week terms each year.

Students get to put those skills to use in two full productions annually at Gorey Little Theatre, giving the weekly classes a clear performance goal to build toward each term.

Covering all three performing arts strands in one school suits students working toward musical theatre in particular, rather than a single specialism.

TEKcentral, based in Harperstown, Wexford, runs hands-on coding classes for children that start with visual tools like Scratch and MakeCode before progressing to text-based languages such as Python and C.

That progression gives children a genuine coding pathway rather than a one-off introductory session, letting them build from block-based logic to real programming syntax as their skills develop.

Classes are kept small, giving each child more individual support and screen time during hands-on coding work.

The Stables, a fitness and wellbeing centre in Gorey, Co. Wexford, runs kids' fitness classes as part of its broader programme of activity for the local community.

Group fitness classes for children typically combine movement games, basic strength and coordination work, and general conditioning in a format that keeps younger participants engaged rather than following an adult-style workout structure.

Being part of an established fitness and wellbeing centre means access to a proper indoor training space alongside the class itself.

Little Artist Club at Wexford Arts Centre on Cornmarket runs weekly hands-on art sessions for children aged 4 to 7, held Saturdays from 10 to 11:15am.

Sessions are tied to the centre's current exhibitions, meaning young artists respond to and are inspired by real, changing artwork on display rather than working from a fixed, repeating curriculum.

That link to a live gallery programme gives the class a slightly different creative starting point each term as the exhibitions change.

Kids & Teen Art Classes in Wexford runs 8-week art courses for students from roughly age 6 up to 18, with classes split into groups by age.

Each class is kept small and supported by a teaching assistant alongside the main tutor, giving students more individual guidance during hands-on art-making.

Courses are priced at €100 per student for the full 8-week run.

Caroline Bergin Art runs beginner-friendly art classes for children aged 5 to 15, based in Gorey, covering painting, drawing and clay work across the programme.

Having all three media within the one class gives children a varied creative diet rather than focusing narrowly on just drawing or just painting.

All materials are provided, so families don't need to source or bring any art supplies before a child's first class.

Kung Fu Kickboxing Wexford teaches children a combination of Kung Fu, kickboxing, self-defence and circuit training, led by chief instructor Bobby O'Neill, who brings over 40 years of experience to the club.

Blending several martial arts disciplines with circuit-style fitness work gives classes variety, mixing technique practice with more general conditioning.

That level of long-standing instructor experience is a notable feature for a children's martial arts club in the area.

Leebow runs weekly art classes for children aged 5 to 13, with each term running 7 weeks and priced at €100.

For younger siblings, a separate toddler class, Art Explorers, runs on Wednesdays, giving families with children of different ages an option to bring both along on the same day if their schedules line up.

The structured 7-week term format gives a defined start and end point, useful for parents planning around school terms and other activities.

Wexford Taekwon-Do Kids runs a development programme for children aged 4 to 8 across two venues, Wexford and Murrintown, with monthly membership priced between €30 and €45.

The programme pairs self-protection skills with character education, aiming to build children's confidence and respect for others alongside the physical taekwondo technique.

Having two separate venues gives families in both Wexford town and Murrintown a nearby class to attend.

RINKA Sligo runs non-competitive children's fitness classes for ages 3 and up, following a year-long curriculum that covers movement skills, sport skills and general wellbeing.

Keeping the format non-competitive suits younger children or those less interested in structured sport, focusing instead on building a broad foundation of physical literacy.

Covering movement, sport skills and wellbeing together over a full year gives a more rounded programme than a class centred on just one sport or skill.

Musical Explorers, run by Sligo Academy of Music, offers music classes for children aged 3 to 6 at Summerhill College, with sessions available on both Fridays and Saturdays.

At €10 per class, it's a low-commitment way for young children to get an early introduction to rhythm, singing and simple instrument play before moving on to more formal instrumental tuition.

Having both a Friday and a Saturday option gives families flexibility around which day suits their weekly schedule best.

Soccer Stars Sligo runs football-based classes for children from 18 months up to 7 years old, split into three groups — Mini Stars, Stripes and Stars — with weekend sessions held at Scoil Ursula.

Starting football skills this early focuses less on formal rules or competition and more on basic movement, ball familiarity and following simple instructions in a group setting.

The three-tier structure lets children move up through the programme as they grow, staying with the same provider from toddlerhood into early school years.

Art Buddyz runs 1.5-hour creative art sessions for children aged 5 to 13 in Sligo, led by Sheelagh Keane.

Programming is designed with sensory, cognitive and social development in mind, not just artistic output — so sessions are built to support a broader range of a child's development alongside the creative work itself.

The longer 1.5-hour session length allows more time for children to fully engage with a project rather than rushing to finish within a shorter class.

Carraig Climbing runs kids' rock climbing classes in Sligo, with additional summer camps available during school holidays.

The focus is on foundational skills from an early age — grip, body positioning and problem-solving on the wall — building a base that supports climbing at any level as children get older.

Climbing offers a different physical challenge to most other kids' activities, combining strength and flexibility with the mental problem-solving of working out a route.

Atlantic Jiu Jitsu Sligo runs a kids' Brazilian Jiu Jitsu class on Saturdays, split into two groups — ages 7-11 and 12-15 — to keep training partners closer in size and experience.

The class focuses on self-defence and coordination, using BJJ's grappling fundamentals to build both practical skills and body awareness.

A single Saturday class keeps the commitment manageable for families while still offering structured, age-appropriate training.

Sligo Taekwon-Do Club runs kids' Taekwon-Do classes for ages 8 to 13 on Mondays, with an additional Friday session available for current junior members wanting extra training time.

Classes place particular emphasis on safety, self-control and respect, values that sit alongside the physical kicking and pattern work central to Taekwon-Do.

The option of a second weekly session for existing juniors gives more committed students a way to progress faster without changing club.

Kenpo Karate Academy on Main Street in Celbridge runs a children's karate programme for ages 4 and up, with confidence and discipline as central themes alongside the physical technique.

Progress is marked through a belt-graduation system, giving children a visible reward and sense of achievement as they advance through the ranks.

That structured progression tends to help keep younger children motivated, since each new belt is a clear, tangible sign of how far they've come.

Orla Gildea School of Speech and Drama runs classes at The Mill in Celbridge every Wednesday, split into a Junior group for ages 5-7 and an Intermediate group for ages 8-12.

Speech and drama training builds public-speaking confidence, clear articulation and performance skills, useful well beyond the drama class itself.

Term fees are €215, covering a full term of weekly Wednesday sessions for whichever age group a child joins.

Sensory Explorers at Celbridge Playzone runs weekly inclusive sensory play sessions every Tuesday from 11am to 12pm, aimed at neurodivergent children and their siblings.

Each session is built around a themed sensory activity, giving structure and variety week to week while keeping the environment welcoming and low-pressure for children who benefit from a more sensory-considered space.

Explicitly including siblings in the session means the whole family can take part together rather than splitting up for separate activities.

Bubbles Play & Music, based at St Wolstan's Abbey in Celbridge, runs a range of classes for children from 6 weeks old up to age 5, including Sensory Baby Play, Play & Learn, Music, Art and Sports.

Covering such a wide span within one provider means families can stay with Bubbles as their child grows, moving from early sensory classes for infants into more active music, art and sports sessions as they approach school age.

Having several class types under one roof also makes it easy to try a different format if one style doesn't suit a particular child.

Celbridge Piano's Keyboard Games course teaches piano to children aged 4 to 7 in small groups of 2 to 4 students, with each class running 30 minutes.

Teaching follows an audiation-based approach, meaning children learn to internalise and 'hear' music before matching it to notation, a method often used to build genuine musicality rather than rote note-reading.

The small group size keeps sessions social while still giving each child meaningful individual attention from the tutor.

The Craft Corner runs after-school art classes at North Kildare Sports Club, serving families around Maynooth and Kilcock, with two groups on offer: a Middle group for 1st to 6th class, and an Advanced group for 3rd to 6th class.

Having an advanced option alongside the general group lets more experienced young artists take on more challenging projects rather than working at the same pace as complete beginners.

The current term runs for 9 weeks in spring, giving a defined block of after-school sessions.

CoderDojo Malahide runs a free kids' computer club on Sundays at the Parish Hall in Malahide, part of the wider volunteer-led CoderDojo movement.

Sessions are booked weekly rather than through a fixed enrolment, with booking links sent out via a mailing list, so interested families need to sign up to stay in the loop on availability.

Being free and community-run makes it an accessible way for children to get hands-on coding experience without the cost of a paid course.

Drama House in Malahide runs musical theatre and youth theatre classes for children aged 4 to 12, structured across Junior, Intermediate and Senior groups.

That three-tier structure gives a clear progression path as children grow, with material and expectations increasing at each stage rather than children of very different ages sharing one class.

Summer camps run during school holidays, offering a more concentrated performing arts experience alongside the regular term-time classes.

East Coast School of Ballet teaches RAD and ISTD ballet to children from age 3, running classes across five different venues in Malahide.

The school describes its environment as non-competitive, keeping the focus on technique, discipline and enjoyment of dance rather than competition results.

Trial lessons are available for families wanting to see whether ballet, and this particular school, is the right fit before committing to a term.

Sketch School Malahide runs creative art classes for children aged 7 to 12 on Saturdays at St. Andrew's Parish Centre, across two terms each year.

All materials are provided as part of the class, so there's nothing extra for parents to buy or bring along before a child's first session.

Running just two terms a year, rather than continuous enrolment, gives a defined start and end to each block of classes.

Clonmel Tuition Academy on Gladstone Street runs beginner French classes for children aged 5 to 12, structured across four levels and delivered in 60-minute weekly sessions over a 10-week course.

The levelled structure gives a clear sense of progression, with children moving from Level 1 through to Level 4 as their vocabulary and confidence with the language build.

Starting a language this young is widely seen as advantageous for developing an ear for pronunciation and general language-learning ability.

Phoenix Strength and Conditioning, on Cashel Road in Clonmel, runs fitness classes for kids and teens built around movement quality rather than simply pushing intensity or repetitions.

That focus on how a movement is performed — proper mechanics for squatting, jumping, running and similar patterns — is intended to build a safer, more capable foundation before young athletes move into heavier training loads.

It suits children and teens looking to build general athleticism, whether or not they're training for a specific sport.

South Tipperary Arts Centre, at 1 Nelson Street in Clonmel, runs art classes and workshops for kids, teens and adults.

Offering classes across such a wide age range under one roof means families can potentially attend alongside each other, or simply have a consistent, familiar venue as children move from a kids' class into teen or adult-level workshops over time.

Being based at an established arts centre gives access to proper studio space and materials as part of the class.

Bunny Hop Music & Movement, run by On Your Toes Clonmel, introduces very young children aged 0 to 4 to rhythm, songs and movement in one combined class.

At this age, classes are typically less about formal instruction and more about shared sensory experience between parent and child, using music as a playful, structured activity.

It offers an early, low-pressure starting point for music exposure well before a child would be ready for individual instrument lessons.
